clue.text: Kind of red figures that count?

definitions.text: Kind of red figures that count?

parts.note: cardinal is a deep scarlet, the colour of a cardinal's robes
figures are numerals or numbers

explanation.surface: A question about which red-clad dignitaries really matter.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines and builds the answer: a shade of red plus figures, read together as the numbers used for counting.
explanation.definitionFit: In mathematics the counting numbers one, two, three are called cardinals, as opposed to ordinals like first and second.

clue.text: Stories told from from Pilgrims' Progress to a place in Kent

definitions.text: Stories told from from Pilgrims' Progress to a place in Kent

parts.note: surface reading: Bunyan's allegory The Pilgrim's Progress
setter's reading: Chaucer's tales told by pilgrims as they progress towards a cathedral city in Kent

explanation.surface: Tales passed on from Bunyan's famous book to somewhere in Kent.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue prints 'from' twice, a slip in the source. Chaucer's pilgrims tell stories on the road to Canterbury, the Kent cathedral city.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaucer's collection is framed as a storytelling contest among pilgrims travelling to the shrine of Becket in Kent.

clue.text: Scoundrel's uniform drenched in dreadful gore

indicators.note: something drenched in a liquid is surrounded by it, so one piece sits inside another
a dreadful mess of a word has its letters thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
U is Uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A villain's outfit soaked in horrible blood.
explanation.definitionFit: A rogue is a dishonest or unprincipled person, a direct synonym for a villain.

clue.text: Fashionable present, for example, that's great

parts.note: in means trendy or fashionable
the present is one example of a grammatical tense

explanation.surface: A trendy gift that's simply wonderful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Present' looks like a gift, but 'for example' shows it is an instance of something: a verb tense.
explanation.definitionFit: Great in the sense of extreme in degree, as in great heat or intense heat.

clue.text: Phials for first of urine sample misplaced

indicators.note: things misplaced are put in the wrong positions, so the letters are reordered
only the opening letter of the following word is wanted

parts.note: the initial letter of urine
taken as written

explanation.surface: Little bottles needed because a urine sample went astray.
explanation.definitionFit: Ampules are small sealed glass vials, typically holding a single dose of medicine, so they are phials.

clue.text: Unaffected note

definitions.meaning: first meaning: without pretension, behaving genuinely
second meaning: in music, a note that is neither sharp nor flat

explanation.surface: A message that stays calm and untouched by events.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means genuine and unpretentious in manner, and in music names a note that is neither sharpened nor flattened.

clue.text: Short skirt, very short, with fur trimming

indicators.note: cut short means the last letter is lopped off the word before it

parts.note: a miniskirt, or mini, is a very short skirt
taken as written, then trimmed of its end

explanation.surface: A tiny skirt, extremely tiny, edged with fur.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' appears twice: the first belongs to the skirt, the second clips the word very.
explanation.definitionFit: Miniver is a plain white fur, historically ermine, used to trim ceremonial robes.

clue.text: New text about traveller being sociable

indicators.note: about means around, so the rearranged letters surround the next piece
a new version of the word has its letters made over in a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
a rover is someone who travels or wanders

explanation.surface: A fresh text message about a traveller who likes company.
explanation.definitionFit: An extrovert is an outgoing person who thrives on company, so the word describes someone sociable.

clue.text: Little time, when inn's closed, perhaps, for a song from a show

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the words are only one possible arrangement of these letters

parts.note: T is the short form of time
taken as written, all fourteen letters

explanation.surface: A short while at closing time at the pub calls for a show tune.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole phrase plus one letter is the fodder; 'perhaps' is easy to read as mere hedging.
explanation.definitionFit: Send in the Clowns is Sondheim's famous ballad from the musical A Little Night Music.

clue.text: Strange thing to see in place of evening entertainment

indicators.note: a strange form of the word is an odd, unfamiliar arrangement of its letters

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
to spot something is to see it

explanation.surface: An odd sight to be found at a club after dark.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightspot is a nightclub or bar, a venue people visit for entertainment after dark.

clue.text: Time in the middle of the day to get off

indicators.note: one piece placed in another sits inside it

parts.note: midday, twelve o'clock
T is the short form of time

explanation.surface: Lunchtime is the moment to step off the bus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get off' sounds like leaving, but the definition is just 'off' in the sense of unacceptable.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying behaviour is a bit off means it is not acceptable, which is exactly the colloquial sense of the answer phrase.

clue.text: Re-let a new building that's permanent

indicators.note: building means constructing, so the letters are put together into something new

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A landlord letting out a fresh building that is here to stay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New building' reads as one phrase, but new supplies a letter and building is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Eternal means lasting for ever, without end, a close synonym for permanent.

clue.text: Artist's fiddle almost conjures up this Italian dish

indicators.note: almost the whole word means it stops one letter short

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, is the standard crossword artist
a fiddle is a violin

explanation.surface: A painter's violin playing nearly conjures up a plate of pasta.
explanation.definitionFit: Ravioli are small square Italian pasta parcels with a filling, served as a dish.

clue.text: Some of the better audio accessories for the period

indicators.note: only part of the following words is needed, a run of letters within them

parts.note: the run straddles the gap between the first two words

explanation.surface: Shopping for upmarket hi-fi extras of a certain vintage.
explanation.definitionFit: An era is a period of history marked by some distinctive character.

clue.text: Poor intelligence produces unfortunate reports

parts.note: poor in quality is bad
intelligence in the sense of information received

explanation.surface: Sloppy spy work leads to grim dispatches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Intelligence' suggests brains, but here it means information.
explanation.definitionFit: Bad news is information that is unwelcome or unlucky, matching reports that are unfortunate.

clue.text: Complaint about Daisy's Personal Equity Plan

indicators.note: about can mean turned around or all over the place, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
PEP was a British tax-free savings scheme, the Personal Equity Plan

explanation.surface: Someone grumbling about Daisy's investment scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: A PEP was a UK tax-free savings plan, replaced by ISAs in 1999. 'Complaint' reads as a grievance but means an ailment.
explanation.definitionFit: Dyspepsia is indigestion, and complaint is a standard word for an illness or medical disorder.

clue.text: Small Scotch

definitions.meaning: second meaning: Scottish, as the word is a Scots one for little

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like ordering a small whisky; instead the word for little is itself Scottish.
explanation.definitionFit: Wee is the Scots word for little, so it both means tiny and is distinctly a Scottish term.

clue.text: Unending generosity by model with the greatest capacity

indicators.note: without an ending, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: largess, also spelt largesse, is generous giving
the Model T was Ford's famous car

explanation.surface: A fashion model's endless openhandedness makes her the most bountiful.
explanation.definitionFit: Largest means biggest in size, so it describes whatever holds the most, or has the greatest capacity.

clue.text: Worker produced article on time

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
T is the short form of time

explanation.surface: An employee wrote a piece and delivered it by the deadline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' just places one piece after the other in a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Worker ants are the sterile females of a colony, so worker is a common crossword term for the insect.

clue.text: It's about teams' lives

parts.note: re means concerning or about
teams in a match are sides

explanation.surface: A story concerning the lives of the players in two teams.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lives' looks like a plural noun, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To reside somewhere is to have one's home there, so the verb is a synonym of dwells.

clue.text: Searches for water right inside but drifts off

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other, enclosed by it

parts.note: dowsing is searching for underground water, often with a forked stick
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A water diviner hunts with a rod but keeps nodding off.
explanation.definitionFit: To drowse is to doze lightly, so it means falling half asleep or drifting off.

clue.text: Sitting with one's half-sister arranged

indicators.note: arranged means set out in a new order
half the following word is kept and the rest dropped

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, then cut in half

explanation.surface: Settling down to sit with your step-sister, as planned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half-sister' reads as a relative, but it means the first half of the word sister.
explanation.definitionFit: A sitting is a single meeting of a body such as a court or parliament, which is a session.

clue.text: Leading light let off alarm …

parts.note: a leading light, a prominent person, is a star

indicators.note: off suggests something gone wrong, so the letters are disordered

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A celebrity sets off an alarm, with the ellipsis leading into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Let off alarm' reads as setting off an alarm; 'alarm' is a verb meaning frighten.
explanation.definitionFit: To startle someone is to give them a sudden fright, which is to alarm them.

clue.text: Sober son administers drugs

parts.note: sedate means calm and serious, sober
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A clean-living son still hands out narcotics.
explanation.definitionFit: To sedate a patient is to give them calming drugs, so the verb means administers drugs.

clue.text: Fan married unhappily

indicators.note: unhappily suggests things going badly, so the letters fall into a different order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A devotee stuck in a miserable marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A fan is an enthusiastic supporter, someone who looks up to and admires a person.

clue.text: … the day before in Madame Veronique

indicators.note: the letters sit within the following words, spanning them

parts.note: the run straddles the gap between the two words

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: Madame Veronique got a fright on the previous day.
explanation.definitionFit: The eve is the day or evening before an event, as in Christmas Eve.

clue.text: Head of unique stud?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the person in charge
second meaning: a boss is a raised knob or stud, and 'the' marks it as one of a kind

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like the master of a single horse-breeding farm. A boss is a round raised ornament, such as on a shield or ceiling.
explanation.definitionFit: The boss is the person in charge, and a boss is also a raised knob or stud; the article makes it singular.

clue.text: Males do, unfortunately, employ an old word for a maid

definitions.text: an old word for a maid

indicators.note: unfortunately implies things went wrong, so the letters end up out of order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Men, regrettably, still hire a domestic servant.
explanation.definitionFit: Damosel is an archaic spelling of damsel, a young unmarried woman or maiden.

clue.text: Spare metre put in waste container

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a skip is a large open bin for building rubbish, a British term
M is the abbreviation for metre

explanation.surface: A leftover metre of something thrown into a rubbish bin.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a skip is a big open metal bin for builders' waste. 'Spare' looks like an adjective, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To skimp is to be stingy or economise, much as one spares expense by using too little.

clue.text: Doesn't gain a pound, initially, on seafood, even salmon.

parts.note: L, from Latin libra, stands for a pound

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter of each word counts

parts.note: the leading letters of these four words

explanation.surface: A dieter stays the same weight eating fish and salmon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Initially' looks like it applies only to the pound, but it governs the four words after it.
explanation.definitionFit: To lose is the opposite of to gain, whether weight or ground, so it means doesn't gain.

clue.text: In winter I've organised a question and answer session

indicators.note: organised means put into a new order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: Someone boasting of arranging a Q&A event during the cold months.
explanation.definitionFit: An interview is a meeting in which one party asks questions and the other answers them.

clue.text: Top actors with lines in Old Glory

parts.note: leading actors are stars
with means together with, and
stripes are lines of colour

explanation.surface: Leading Hollywood actors read their scripts draped in the American flag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lines' suggests an actor's script, but here it means bands of colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Old Glory is a nickname for the flag of the United States, known for its stars and stripes.
